summary_1line: Vasudeva explains the many forms, names, and cosmic roles of Rudra–Mahadeva, describing him as the supreme, multiform deity underlying creation, destruction, and all existence.

image_candidates.scene_text: Indra raises his thunderbolt to strike a mysterious child on Parvati’s lap, but his arm suddenly freezes in midair.
The gods stand bewildered around the radiant child with five locks of hair resting on Parvati’s lap, while Brahma realizes the child is Mahadeva.
Rudra in a cosmic form with countless eyes and many shapes pervades the universe, embodying fire, moon, sun, and all directions.
